text:
sophia: Quick sync 16: new prototype in Figma for compact badges + sampled-region overlay: https://www.figma.com/file/abc. Main questions: 1) while dragging the scrubber over sampled buckets, should the mini-legend update continuously or only after release? 2) visual treatment for sampled vs unsampled ranges (hatched vs outline). Also noticed low contrast on the mini-legend labels.

jamal: For pointer drag I prefer live updates (feels snappy). For keyboard we should avoid flooding the UI/state. Suggest live updates with a small debounce (200-300ms) and commit on Enter/Escape. Keep layout stable so numbers update without shifting components.

ara: Accessibility: continuous updates are okay if we don't spam screen readers. Use aria-live="polite" and only update the live region after a final selection when possible. Contrast: the mini-legend label color at ~#666 is below AA on our background. Bump to #2f3a44 or increase weight.

tal: Copy tweaks: change "Sampling 1/10" to "Sampling: 10%" (shorter, clearer). The top CTA currently styled like a primary button but it's a link; either change semantic to button or make it visually subtle. Also, the tooltip for p95 should read "p95 latency" not "p95 value".

sophia: Proposal: during drag show condensed numeric badges (fixed-width container) that update live; on mouseup/keyboard commit, expand to full legend with labels and units. For sampled regions, prototype shows a light diagonal hatch (12px lines, 35% opacity). Does that feel too noisy?

jamal: Not noisy if we limit opacity and avoid motion. Implementation tip: keep the scrubber overlay a composited layer (will avoid layout thrash), and only repaint numbers. Also, throttle analytics events from scrubbing to 1/sec.

design-bot: Automated check: .mini-legend .label contrast fails WCAG AA. Recommendation: swap to #2f3a44 or set font-weight 600.

ara: UX tweak: when sampling is enabled, add a small toggle to legend "Show sampled overlay" so users can turn it off. Also for keyboard users, offer a text-only indicator (e.g., "sampled" badge) because hatch patterns don't help non-visual users.

sophia: Good call 1; I'll add the toggle and keyboard affordance. One more open question: should preset time ranges auto-snap the scrubber (hard jump) or only hint the user? I lean toward hinting to avoid surprising shifts during exploratory analysis.

tal: Agree on hint only. Offer an explicit "Snap to preset" in settings for power users.

jamal: I'll spike an experiment: debounced live updates + keyboard commit, stable layout, sampled-overlay toggle. Will share a short perf note after.

sophia: Thanks 18. I'll update the Figma, write three tickets: DESIGN-4910 (contrast + legend badges), DESIGN-4911 (scrubber behavior + keyboard commit), DESIGN-4912 (sampled overlay + toggle).
